question: Directive (EU) 2019/904 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment was adopted on 5 June 2019. Subject to a number of limited exceptions, Member States had to transpose these new rules, which are essential for protecting the environment, by July 2021. 1.
Have all Member States now correctly transposed this directive correctly?
Will Member States that have not yet done so be penalised?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.5.2024) The Commission is committed to ensure a coordinated and consistent transposition of the Single-Use Plastics Directive (SUPD)1. Member States had to transpose this Directive into national legislation by July 2021 and the Commission is in the process of verifying their compliance. All Member States had to notify their transposing provisions to the Commission.

As a first step, the Commission checked the completeness of these notifications and then opened in 20222 infringement proceedings against eleven Member States for not having fully transposed the Directive into their national laws. All except three of those cases (regarding Belgium, Denmark and Finland) have been closed in the meantime.

As a second step, in 2023 the Commission started conformity checking of the national measures transposing the SUPD in the Member States. Depending on the outcome of this assessment, the Commission will decide how to proceed.
1 Directive (EU) 2019/904 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on the reduction of the
impact of certain plastic products on the environment, OJ L 155, 12.6.2019, p. 1–19. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_22_5402
